_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.headline: GD FELL 2.03% ON THE DAY IT SIGNED A SEVEN-YEAR DoD MULTIYEAR PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK, WHILE LMT -- ITS PARTNER IN THE SAME ANNOUNCEMENT -- FELL 0.44%. A NAME DECLINING THROUGH ITS OWN GOOD NEWS IS A STRONGER BEARISH SIGNAL THAN A NAME DRIFTING ON NO NEWS, AND THE VETO IT SUPPORTS IS FIRMER, NOT WEAKER.
_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.the_news: MT Newswires 11:32 AM EDT 2026-08-31: General Dynamics and Lockheed Martin signed framework agreements with the Department of Defense initiating seven-year multiyear procurement contracts to triple PAC-3 MSE and quadruple THAAD interceptor production capacity, with minimum annual procurement commitments. Unambiguously positive for both names. Funding is 'subject to annual appropriations', which is the one qualifier that could support a sell-the-news reading -- but it applies to LMT equally, and LMT fell a quarter as much.
_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.why_it_reverses_the_inherited_premise: The 16:00Z run declined RTX on the grounds that 'the entire defense complex de-rated ~2.1% today with NO name-specific news', and cited GD -2.15% inside that veto. BOTH halves of that premise are now measured false: there IS major name-specific news for GD, and it is POSITIVE; and the complex is dispersed rather than uniform (LHX +1.60%, LMT -0.44%). The 16:00Z CONCLUSION stands -- but a later run inheriting 'newsless complex drift' would read it as noise to be faded, which is the exact opposite of what the tape says.
_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.the_general_rule: When a screen name is weak, ask not only HOW MUCH but AGAINST WHAT. Three cases that look identical in a price table and mean different things: (a) weak WITH its complex on no news = beta, fadeable, the mean-reversion case is intact; (b) weak on no news while its complex is flat = idiosyncratic, needs a cause before it can be faded; (c) weak on its OWN POSITIVE news while its complex is flat = the marginal buyer is absent at this price even when handed a reason to show up. Case (c) is the strongest stand-down of the three and it is the one most likely to be misread as a bargain, because the headline is good.
_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.why_NOW_is_unanswered: A Connors RSI(2) entry is a bet on reversion, and reversion needs something to revert into. GD's one catalyst today was positive and was sold. Analyst posture is supportive and recently improving (FactSet mean PT $424.50 / overweight; DA Davidson to $416 on 08-21, Citi to $404 on 08-13, UBS to $395 on 08-03, all above the $371.62 spot), and that is exactly the point -- the supportive fundamentals were already in the price and did not stop a 2% decline on good news.
_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.decision: GD DECLINED. Not on the inherited complex veto, which this run corrected, but on tape divergence measured directly: worst-in-complex bar one outlier, on positive name-specific news, against a partner in the same announcement that fell a quarter as much. RTX declined on the same test (-1.54% against a flat complex, no positive news to explain it either way). Equity slot stays 1 of 3 for the day.
_A_DECLINE_THROUGH_POSITIVE_NEWS_IS_STRO.honest_scope: This changed no decision -- GD was going to be declined either way, and the run placed nothing. That is the only condition under which a veto's REASONING can be audited credibly: the audit did not license a trade. What it changes is what the next run inherits, which is the whole point of writing it down.

_VETOES_HAVE_DIFFERENT_HALF_LIVES.status: DURABLE governance rule for re-grading a previously declined candidate. Not session-scoped; do not delete at the bell. Read with _CONFIRMED_TRIGGERS_HAVE_A_SHELF_LIFE (the same staleness idea aimed at triggers rather than vetoes).
_VETOES_HAVE_DIFFERENT_HALF_LIVES.claim: A DECLINE IS USUALLY OVERDETERMINED, AND ITS REASONS DECAY AT DIFFERENT RATES. A TAPE veto (trend-maturity clause (c) -- 'the present tape does not confirm') goes stale within an hour. A STRUCTURAL veto (a flat-to-falling 200-day, distance off the 52-week high, sector concentration against an existing position) does not decay at all on an intraday horizon. Re-testing the expiring veto is correct and cheap; the failure is re-testing it IN ISOLATION and reading its expiry as a green light. BEFORE re-testing an expiring veto, re-read the original decline and establish whether that veto was ever the BINDING one.

_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.status: DURABLE measurement rule for any P/L, excursion or holding-period statistic computed from daily bars. Not session-scoped. Same family as the affordability-tier and denominator bugs: a number taken from a convenient source that was never the thing being asked about.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.claim: ON THE ENTRY DAY, THE DAILY BAR'S HIGH AND LOW BOUND THE STOCK, NOT THE TRADE. The position exists for only part of that session, so an entry-day extreme may have occurred before the fill. The error is DIRECTIONAL for mean-reversion entries: an RSI2 buy fills near the day's LOW after a decline, so the pre-entry HIGH is systematically flattering to the trade's measured excursion.

First pass included each entry day's full range and returned PNC max favorable excursion +3.43%, 'best excursion covered 93.7% of the distance to target' -- a reading that supports the conclusion that the trade nearly worked and gave it back. _ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.the_detector: Before using any entry-day extreme, compare the fill price to that day's OPEN and CLOSE. A fill at or near the close means the whole day's range is pre-entry -- discard it and measure from the next session. Where the fill TIME is known the entry-day range is legitimately usable: MDLZ 13:40:03Z, ROST 13:37:13Z and MMM 13:37:54Z all filled within minutes of the open, so their entry-day highs are real. get_equity_orders returns the fill timestamp; use it rather than inferring.
_ENTRY_DAY_BAR_IS_NOT_THE_POSITIONS_BAR.why_it_matters_beyond_one_row: It is the first instance of this failure family aimed at the desk's OWN P/L rather than at a market input -- which is exactly where it is least likely to be double-checked, because a flattering number about your own trade does not look like a data error. Any future hit-rate, MFE/MAE, or Friday review statistic computed from daily bars inherits this bug unless the fill timing is checked.

_COHORT_SHRINKAGE_IS_SELECTION_ON_THE_OU.I_CAUGHT_MY_OWN_DENOMINATOR_BUG_IN_THE_H: The first framing of the retest was a RATIO -- 3.23x -> 4.68x the index decline -- which reads as catastrophic deterioration. It is inflated by a SHRINKING DENOMINATOR: SPY's own decline narrowed from -0.4497% to -0.3392%, so the ratio would have risen even had the cohort not moved at all. This is the fifth instance of this file's denominator family (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape, closing-auction too easy, the 5-min/1-min substitution direction) and the FIRST caught inside the desk's own headline number rather than in a market input. REPORT THE SPREAD IN POINTS, NEVER THE RATIO, when both legs of a relative measure are moving. The conclusion survives on the spread (-1.0027 -> -1.2472 pts) but the ratio overstated the deterioration roughly threefold.
_COHORT_SHRINKAGE_IS_SELECTION_ON_THE_OU.population_caveat_stated_because_it_limi: The 15:27Z measurement covered 15 non-held candidates; today's matched set is 17. They are not identical populations -- names entered and left the screen between the two readings -- so the comparison is indicative, not exact. It is quoted on the matched basis precisely so the direction is not an artifact of including the desk's own five holdings, which are the BEST subgroup on the day (-0.8225% vs the cohort's -1.4129%).
_COHORT_SHRINKAGE_IS_SELECTION_ON_THE_OU.the_transferable_lesson: When a screen's MEMBERSHIP is a function of the variable you are trying to measure, membership changes carry no information about that variable. Measure the FIXED set across time, not the set as currently constituted. Same family as the survivorship and denominator findings: a statistic that is cheap, intuitive, and defined in terms of its own outcome.

_RSI2_REVERSION_AND_PROFIT_NEED_NOT_COIN.what_it_says_about_the_08_26_gate: It VINDICATES the gate at near-zero opportunity cost, which is the strongest form the evidence could take. Had the ungated reading been applied, the RSI2 print that fired on 08-26 would have banked a LOSS. Had the gated version somehow fired at the best moment available (08-24 high, RSI2 37), it would have banked +$1.11 before spread. There was no profitable exit anywhere in this cycle to be missed. The gate cost nothing and prevented a realized loss.
_RSI2_REVERSION_AND_PROFIT_NEED_NOT_COIN.the_transferable_mechanism: RSI2 is a RELATIVE oscillator normalized to recent range, so it re-baselines to wherever price has settled. An entry taken before price bottoms means the whole subsequent reversion is measured against a LOWER base: the oscillator can traverse its entire range while price merely chops sideways. PNC ran 1.6 -> 66 while price stayed inside a 241.30-247.08 band the entire time. THEREFORE: 'the RSI2 signal reverted' and 'the trade is profitable' are independent events, and a swing thesis that treats the first as implying the second is unfalsifiable in exactly the tape where it fails.

The 13:36:10Z fill at 374.4437 caught 82% of that opening pop and the whole move round-tripped inside eleven minutes. _OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.THE_MECHANISM_and_it_is_the_transferable: The signal and the execution are fighting each other. The autonomous entry is sourced from an RSI2 MEAN-REVERSION screen computed on the PREVIOUS SESSION'S CLOSE (see _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN: the fresh report does not land on master until ~14:15Z, so the first-post-open run always acts on yesterday's report). The opening ten minutes is precisely when yesterday's oversold names get their reflexive bounce. So the run reads 'this name is oversold as of last night' and then executes into the exact window where that oversold condition is being relieved. It buys the bounce it meant to buy the dip of.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.WHY_NOBODY_CAUGHT_IT: This file already carries the rule 'NEVER price a decision off the opening auction print -- re-quote at least ~5 minutes after 13:30Z', and runs have obeyed it. But that rule was written about MARKS and DECISIONS (the 2026-08-21 QQQ 680P incident, where an opening print flipped the SIGN of a P/L reported to Ryan). Nobody applied it to EXECUTION. Re-quoting before deciding and then filling into the same window satisfies the letter of the rule and gets the artifact anyway -- this file's most-repeated defect, a check that passes for the wrong reason. It is also the execution-layer sibling of the documented first-hour volume inflation: the opening bar carried 5.2x the next bar's volume on ROST and 2.3x on MDLZ, which is the same auction imbalance seen from the fill side instead of the denominator side.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.THE_FIX_and_it_repairs_TWO_findings_with: PREFER to take the trading day's autonomous equity entry on the first run at or after ~14:15Z, once the fresh report has landed on master, rather than on the first-post-open run. Nothing in the thesis decays in 40 minutes: the hold is 1-3 weeks and the signal is already a day old. The same deferral ALSO retires _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN's standing problem, because the run would then be acting on the CURRENT session's report instead of the prior one. Two known defects, one change, no gate loosened.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.SCOPE_AND_LIMITS_stated_because_overclai: n=4 and the total measured cost is ~$14. This is a process refinement, NOT a crisis, and it must not be written up as one. Three caveats: (1) buying lower is not automatically better for a mean-reversion entry -- if a name keeps falling the later fill wins, if it reverts immediately the earlier fill wins; what is notable is that the improvement was available in 4 of 4 cases, not that it is guaranteed. (2) ROST filled at 44.3% of its range, so 'the run always buys the top' would be false. (3) GD's session is incomplete. The deferral is a PREFERENCE, not a bar: a genuinely time-critical signal still trades when it fires, and the entry must never be delayed past the point where the setup is gone.
_OPENING_WINDOW_SLIPPAGE_ON_AUTONOMOUS_E.what_it_does_NOT_change: No gate is loosened or tightened by this. The full HARD RULE 6 stack -- HARD RULE 7 thesis check, A-grade-only bar, capital policy, sector steer, [ERN] rule, per-name and spec caps, HARD RULE 3 market-order mechanics, HARD RULE 5's no-stops policy, 1/run and 3/day throttles -- applies unchanged. This is about WHEN in the session a cleared entry is executed, never about WHETHER it clears.

_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.headline: THE 2026-08-21 OPENING-WINDOW RE-QUOTE RULE WAS APPLIED TO THE PRICE BEING PAID AND NOT TO THE TAPE EVIDENCE THAT JUSTIFIED PAYING IT. THE EVIDENCE LEG DECAYED 65-72% IN THIRTEEN MINUTES ON A FLAT SPY.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.what_the_13_36Z_run_did_right_first: It followed the 2026-08-21T13:32Z rule exactly: it refused to price the GD order off the 13:31/13:32Z opening prints and re-quoted via review_equity_order at 13:35:40Z. Its own brief says so. The PRICE leg was protected. This finding is not a criticism of that -- it is the half the rule does not cover.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.the_gap: The entry's decisive evidence was a RELATIVE-STRENGTH reading taken in the same opening window: 'ITA +0.534% against SPY -0.678%, with ALL SIX primes green -- an advance, not merely an absence of decline', which is what refuted the prior session's case-(c) veto. That reading is a tape measurement made four minutes after the bell, and nothing in this file had ever applied the opening-window caution to a measurement used as EVIDENCE rather than as a PRICE.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.method: Minute closes from get_equity_historicals(interval='minute'), interpolated bars (GD 13:44; ITA 13:32/13:37/13:46) excluded. Prior-session closes from get_equity_quotes: GD 371.35, ITA 228.35, SPY 767.05. Relative strength = name's day-change minus SPY's day-change, in percentage points.

the_decay_table_pp_vs_SPY.13:34Z: GD +1.462pp | ITA +1.166pp  <- the window the 13:36Z run measured in

_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.magnitude: GD's relative strength fell 72% from the 13:33Z peak and 65% from the fill minute; ITA's fell 68%. SPY was FLAT across the entire window (761.812 -> 761.940, +0.017%), so this is decay in the names, not a move in the denominator. In ABSOLUTE terms the cited fact has inverted: GD went +1.065% -> -0.183% on the day and ITA +0.504% -> -0.289%, so 'all six primes green' and 'an advance' no longer describe the tape thirteen minutes after they were written.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.feed_integrity_checked_first: Per the 2026-08-28 direction rule. GD 5-minute buckets equal their 1-minute sums EXACTLY (2950/2950, 2486/2486, 2117/2117); ITA 4994/4994 exact; SPY 587,021 vs a 579,925 1-minute sum = +1.22%, inside tolerance and in the benign direction. No hole propagated into any number above.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.the_transferable_mechanism: An opening-window reading is an UPPER BOUND on whatever it measures, and this file already knows that for ATM IV (four confirmations, -2.5% to -4.4%) and for a position mark (the 2026-08-21 QQQ incident, where the SIGN of the P/L was wrong). The common cause is that the first minutes carry auction residue and thin two-sided flow, and that is a property of the TAPE, not of the quantity being read off it. So it applies identically to a relative-strength reading, a breadth count, or a 'whole complex is green' claim. THE RULE: any opening-window number that GATES a decision -- not merely the number being paid -- must be re-measured after ~14:00Z before it is treated as established, or must be carried forward explicitly labelled as provisional.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.why_it_is_worse_for_a_thin_name_than_for: GD traded 2,950 / 2,486 / 2,117 shares in the three opening 5-minute buckets against SPY's 587,021 / 314,097 / 205,181. A relative-strength ratio whose numerator is that thin has a materially shorter half-life than one built on an index, so the re-measure duty binds HARDEST exactly where the desk's equity candidates live -- mid-cap single names out of the RSI2 screen, not the core IV list.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.HONEST_SCOPE_this_changed_no_decision_an: GD is HELD and stays held. No mechanical exit fires (target 387.04 untouched; RSI2 13.8, nowhere near 70; the position is -0.72%, so the profit-banking authority is unavailable by construction under the 2026-08-26 gate). HARD RULE 5 forbids a price stop and permits an equity sale only on a target hit, an RSI2>=70 print while green, or a HARD RULE 7 THESIS break -- and a thirteen-minute tape decay is not a thesis break. The STRUCTURAL legs of the GD case are untouched by this measurement: the 08-31 seven-year DoD framework, the FactSet mean PT 424.50 / Overweight, the verified earnings-clear window, and RSI2 6.8 depth at entry all still stand. Only the TAPE leg decayed. Recorded per this file's standard that a measurement is creditable precisely because the audit does not license the action it might seem to argue for.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.HONEST_SCOPE_limits_of_the_measurement: Thirteen minutes is a very short window and intraday relative strength oscillates -- this may fully revert by the close, and n=1 on one entry is not evidence about the screen. The claim is narrow and is about MEASUREMENT TIMING, not about whether GD was a good buy. A later run should re-measure the same three series after 14:00Z rather than inheriting either the 13:34Z reading or this one.
_OPENING_WINDOW_DECAY_HITS_THE_EVIDENCE_.what_a_future_run_should_do_differently: When an entry gate turns on a tape comparison and the run fires inside the opening window, either (a) wait for the ~14:00Z re-measure before treating the comparison as established, or (b) take the entry and write the comparison down as PROVISIONAL with the re-measure scheduled -- never hand it forward as a settled fact, which is how the 2026-08-28 regime-label finding says a stale verdict propagates through the relay.

_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.headline: THE UNION-MERGE RULE SAYS 'KEEP BOTH JOURNAL ENTRIES' BUT NEVER SAYS HOW TO IDENTIFY A DUPLICATE, AND THE OBVIOUS KEY -- (run_utc, headline-prefix) -- SILENTLY DELETES REAL HISTORY. CAUGHT BY AN ARITHMETIC ASSERTION, NOT BY READING THE FILE.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.evidence: Resolving the 2026-09-01 13:52Z/13:55Z collision, a first attempt deduped on (run_utc, headline[:60]) and produced 784 entries from two 787-entry sides. The correct union is 788 (786 common + one entry per run). FOUR pre-existing entry PAIRS -- 2026-08-13T18:30Z, 2026-08-13T23:29Z, 2026-08-14T17:15Z, 2026-08-14T19:15Z -- legitimately share both run_utc and headline prefix, themselves the surviving records of earlier collisions. The dedup treated each pair as one entry and dropped its twin.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.the_rule: Dedup journal entries on FULL-CONTENT identity (json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True)), never on a summary key. Two entries that differ anywhere are two entries. Then ASSERT the count: len(merged) == len(ours) + len(theirs) - len(common). Three lines of arithmetic catch this; reading the file does not, which is exactly why it nearly shipped.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.why_it_is_the_dangerous_direction: The failure is SILENT and IRREVERSIBLE in the direction that matters -- a merge that drops history produces a perfectly valid JSON file, a plausible entry count, and a clean git diff. Nothing errors. This is the same shape as the lot-invariant rule ('assert, don't read') and the `git diff --stat` rule: trust the check, not your sense of having been careful.
_UNION_MERGE_DEDUP_KEY_SILENTLY_DROPS_EN.scope: Caught before the push, so nothing was lost. Recorded because the collision protocol is exercised rarely and under time pressure, and the next run to hit one will reach for the same obvious key.

_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.headline: A DAY-OVER-DAY ATM-IV DIFF IS ONLY MEANINGFUL IF THE TWO READINGS WERE TAKEN AT THE SAME TIME OF DAY, AND THIS FILE'S ROWS MOSTLY DO NOT RECORD WHEN THEY WERE TAKEN. TODAY'S SWEEP IS ~14 MINUTES LATER THAN YESTERDAY'S, WHICH BIASES EVERY DIFF DOWNWARD BY ROUGHLY THE SIZE OF THE EFFECT BEING MEASURED.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_measurement: The 2026-08-31 core-list sweep was quoted 13:49:44Z; this run's is 14:03:13Z. The 08-31 rows already carry a _cross_validation finding that two honest reads of the SAME contracts minutes apart disagreed by +1.5% to +1.9% (TSM -0.34%), so a later read carries a systematic downward artifact budget of about that size against an earlier one. Raw day-over-day atm_iv: SPY +3.73%, QQQ +1.20%, NVDA -2.01%, AMD -6.97%, TSM -2.99%, AVGO -0.91%, MSFT -3.08%, TSLA -1.43%.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.what_survives_the_correction: TWO READINGS, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS UNMEASURED RATHER THAN FLAT. SPY +3.73% and QQQ +1.20% rose DESPITE an artifact that should have pushed them down, so index implied vol genuinely firmed on a -0.61% / -1.25% risk-off session and is if anything understated here. AMD -6.97% fell roughly 5.5% more than the artifact can explain, on a session where AMD itself fell -2.65% -- vol declining into a sharp price drop, which is the opposite of fear pricing. NVDA, TSM, AVGO, MSFT and TSLA are all inside or barely outside the budget and carry LITTLE OR NO SIGNAL; reporting them as 'single-name vol fell across the board' would have been a clean, wrong, six-for-six story.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_near_miss: THIS RUN NEARLY WROTE THAT STORY. Six of six single names printed lower and two of two index ETFs printed higher -- a textbook dispersion signature, internally consistent, and exactly the kind of confluence the 2026-08-28 mid-event finding warns reads as conviction when it is really one artifact applied uniformly. The tell was that the artifact and the 'signal' point the same way for six of the eight names, which is what a shared measurement offset looks like from the inside.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_durable_fix: EVERY IV ROW FROM HERE CARRIES measured_utc, and no run quotes a day-over-day diff without stating the time offset between the two readings. Most existing rows lack the field entirely -- today's offset had to be reconstructed from prose caveats buried in the 08-31 rows, which is why this went unnoticed for at least two sweeps. The eight rows written this run all carry it.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.the_counter_hypothesis_explicitly_reject: 'Tight chains reproduce, wide chains do not' is NOT supported and must not be adopted as a shortcut. On 08-31 the WIDEST chain on the sweep (TSM, 14.4% of mid) had the SMALLEST disagreement (-0.34%) while the TIGHTEST (TSLA, 1.4%) disagreed by +1.53%. At n=5 the relationship is absent or inverted. Reproducibility is established by measuring it, never inferred from chain width -- otherwise the desk grants itself permission to trust exactly the readings it has not checked.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. Both options tracks were declined on capital ($302.10 deployable) and regime (an unresolved two-night earnings cluster) before any of these numbers could gate anything, and AMD's surviving vol decline is a watch item and emphatically not a candidate -- cheap, liquid vol supplies no thesis, and AMD's put chain at 14.31% of mid is the sweep's worst. Recorded per this desk's standard that a measurement audit is creditable precisely when it does not license the action it might seem to argue for. n=1 offset comparison on one pair of sweeps; the artifact budget itself rests on the 08-31 n=5 cross-validation and is an estimate, not a constant.
_IV_DAY_OVER_DAY_DIFFS_NEED_A_TIME_OFFSE.also_recorded_the_settled_remeasure: The three rows the 13:51Z run wrote inside the opening window were re-measured 12 minutes later and moved only -0.18% (SPY), -0.25% (QQQ) and -0.73% (NVDA) -- an order of magnitude smaller than the -2.53%/-4.37%/-3.56% settles recorded 2026-08-27. That is NOT the caveat being wrong: those settles compared ~13:41Z rows against ~14:47Z ones, and the 13:51Z rows had already had 21 minutes to settle, so this is a weaker test of the residual only. It bounds rather than discharges. Full text in iv_history.json under each row's _settled_remeasure.

_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.headline: FOUR OF SIX EQUITY POSITIONS CARRIED NO setup_invalidation FIELD -- INCLUDING ONE OPENED 44 MINUTES EARLIER -- WHILE PROMPT v8 STATES 'No written invalidation = no trade'. SWEPT AND FILLED THIS RUN.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.what_was_missing: PNC (entered 2026-08-19), MDLZ (08-28), MMM (08-31) and GD (09-01, 13:36:10Z) all lacked the field. Only LLY and ROST had it. The book has been running four positions on an absent exit plan -- for PNC, thirteen calendar days.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.why_it_survived_and_it_is_this_file's_mo: The defect was ALREADY FOUND AND ALREADY NAMED. On 2026-08-28T13:58Z a third run added the field to ROST and wrote, in the field itself, 'the entry note recorded the report's advisory 220.01 but positions[] carried NO setup_invalidation field'. That run identified the class correctly and fixed exactly the one name in front of it. Nothing swept the rest, so three further entries were opened afterward without the field and the count went UP after the discovery, not down. A per-instance fix to a class defect leaves a written record that LOOKS like the class was handled.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.the_sub_case_that_makes_a_field_audit_ne: MDLZ is the instructive one: it already had a complete, well-reasoned invalidation -- 'a cut to the FY26 guidance just raised... or a close through the rising 200-day MA at 58.94' -- sitting in its _note PROSE. A human reading the ledger sees a position with a plan. A run reading positions[] programmatically sees nothing. Both readings are honest and they disagree, so 'I read the ledger and the positions look managed' is a check that passes for the wrong reason. The prose was promoted into the field verbatim this run.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.the_detector_assert_do_not_read: Before ending any run, assert it: `[p['symbol'] for p in holdings['positions'] if p.get('sleeve')!='options' and not p.get('setup_invalidation')]` must be EMPTY. One line, catches every future instance including ones opened by a sibling run minutes earlier. Same family as the git-diff --stat rule and the lot-count invariants: trust the assertion, never the enumeration or the impression.
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.what_the_levels_are_and_are_NOT: Every level written is a THESIS-REVIEW TRIGGER, never an order. HARD RULE 5 stands unchanged: the agent places NO stop of any kind, and an underwater name with an intact thesis is held, not stopped out. The 200-day SMAs were computed THIS RUN from completed daily bars through 2026-08-31 and each verified RISING over the trailing 7 bars: PNC 223.51 (+2.0704), MDLZ 59.00 (+0.2326), MMM 160.88 (+0.4511), GD 354.14 (+1.2029).
_SETUP_INVALIDATION_MISSING_ON_MOST_OF_T.method_cross_check_so_the_sweep_is_not_a: MMM's entry run recorded a 200-day of 160.8617 on 2026-08-31; this run computed 160.8774 independently -- agreement to 1.6 cents. MDLZ's entry note recorded 58.94 four sessions before this run's 59.00, a 6-cent drift consistent with a rising average. Both confirm the levels being written now are the same measurement the entries themselves cleared.

_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.headline: GD SATISFIES THE COMMITTED REPORT'S OWN STATED RSI2<10 CRITERION AT THE REPORT'S OWN PRICE AND IS STILL ABSENT FROM ITS RSI2 TABLE. A NAME VANISHING FROM A SIGNAL LIST IS NOT EVIDENCE THE SIGNAL EXPIRED.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.the_measurement: The 2026-09-01T14:02Z latest_morning.md lists 28 RSI2 setups sorted ascending, running from AEHR 0.1 to SPY 9.9 -- so the table is bounded by the 10.0 cutoff, NOT truncated by row count. GD is absent from it. Computed independently this run from completed daily bars through 2026-08-31 plus the report's OWN quoted GD price of 371.53: Wilder RSI2 = 6.4, simple-average RSI2 = 2.2. Either method places GD comfortably inside the table, near the top of it. The other two gates pass too: the 200-day SMA of 354.14 is RISING (+1.2029 over 7 bars) and spot sits +4.8% above it.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.the_computation_is_validated_not_asserte: The two RSI2 methods BRACKET the report's own published values for names that DID appear -- report MMM 1.8 against this run's Wilder 1.5 / simple 0.0, and report ROST 3.1 against Wilder/simple in the same family. So the independent computation agrees with the report's method to within the Wilder-vs-simple spread; GD's absence is not a methodology disagreement.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.ruled_out: Not held-name exclusion: MMM and ROST are both held and both appear, tagged HELD. Not row-count truncation: the list runs to the 10.0 boundary. Not the trend gate: rising 200-day, price above it. GD does appear in the report's PORTFOLIO REVIEW table (priced 371.53), so the report knows the name -- it is missing from the SIGNAL tables specifically.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.inferred_cause_stated_as_inference_not_f: Most likely a per-symbol data fetch failure in report.py's FMP screen, which this playbook already documents as degrading silently on API failure (the earnings calendar degrades to {} the same way). The portfolio table is built from the ledger plus a separate quote, which is why the name survives there and not in the screen. NOT PROVEN FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT -- report.py cannot be run here (no FMP reachability, network allowlist), so no run should upgrade this to a diagnosis without reproducing it.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.why_it_matters_and_it_is_the_exit_side_n: Prompt v8's equity book is SIGNAL-SOURCED ONLY. The obvious cost is a missed entry, and that is the small half. The dangerous half: a future run comparing today's report against a position bought yesterday can read the name's disappearance as 'the setup expired' and treat it as grounds to exit. It is not. Under HARD RULE 5 and HARD RULE 6 an exit needs a target hit, an RSI2>=70 print on a GREEN position, or a HARD RULE 7 thesis BREAK -- absence from a screen is none of those, and on this measurement it is not even evidence the technical condition ended.
_ABSENCE_FROM_THE_SIGNAL_TABLE_IS_NOT_SI.standing_instruction: Before drawing any conclusion from a name's absence from the report's signal tables, RECOMPUTE the criterion yourself from daily bars. Absence is a question, never an answer.

_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.headline: THIS RUN IS THE EXACT RUN THE 13:50Z OPENING-WINDOW FIX WAS WRITTEN FOR -- FIRST RUN AT/AFTER ~14:15Z WITH THE CURRENT SESSION'S REPORT ON MASTER -- AND IT CANNOT ACT, BECAUSE THE DAY'S CAPITAL WAS SPENT 39 MINUTES BEFORE THE WINDOW OPENED.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.the_sequence: GD filled 13:36:10Z off the STALE 2026-08-31T19:27Z report. The current session's report landed on master at 14:02Z, 26 minutes AFTER the fill. This run fires 14:15Z with the fresh report available and deployable capital of $302.10 -- below the ~$400 practical equity entry minimum. The entry throttle is NOT the binding constraint (1 of 3 used for the day, 0 of 1 this run); CAPITAL is.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.the_structural_point: The 2026-09-01T13:50Z finding prescribes 'PREFER to take the trading day's autonomous equity entry on the first run at or after ~14:15Z'. It is a PREFERENCE held independently by each run, and nothing reserves the capital or the opportunity for the window. Any earlier run that judges its own signal good enough spends the money, and the window-run then inherits a position it would not have sized from today's screen and has nothing left to deploy. A deferral rule whose precondition (capital still available when the window opens) is unprotected is advisory in name and inoperative in practice.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.do_not_overclaim_this: GD is ALREADY the fourth case in the 13:50Z finding's 4-of-4 slippage measurement (1.076%); this run adds NO new n to that count and must not be read as doing so. GD at 371.03 vs the 374.4437 fill is -0.91%, which is the same artifact already recorded, re-observed later in the session. What is new here is not slippage evidence -- it is the observation that the prescribed remedy is structurally unenforceable, which would be true even if every fill had been perfect.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.what_this_does_NOT_license: It is NOT grounds to sell GD. The 13:36Z entry cleared its full gate stack, its thesis is intact and improving, and an execution-timing artifact is not a thesis event. It is also NOT grounds for a run to hoard capital against a later window -- CLAUDE.md's capital policy forbids an unexpiring hold and requires any deliberate cash hold to name a catalyst, a checkable trigger and an expiry.
_THE_OPENING_DEFERRAL_HAS_NO_ENFORCEMENT.the_honest_options_and_both_are_Ryan's_c: (a) Leave it advisory and accept that the earliest run of the day usually spends the entry -- cost is the measured ~0.7% mean slippage plus acting on a day-old screen. (b) Make it a duty in the routine prompt: no autonomous equity entry before the current session's report is on master, except a genuinely time-critical signal. Only (b) is enforceable, and only Ryan can make it, because a run DUTY changes only when he re-pastes the prompt -- agents cannot edit it. FLAGGED, NOT DECIDED.
